en: In the sovereign of lotuses, the sovereign of Garuḍas, the sovereign of Viriñca, the sovereign of the kings of gods,
the sovereign of the three worlds, the sovereign of all sovereigns—
May my mind delight in the Lord of Śrīraṅgam. || 1 ||
To her who has the color of a blue lotus, whose ears are filled by her arms, whose eyes reach to her ears, who is the consort of Kamala,
who is the beautiful arena of Śrī, and who has conquered the arena of wrestlers.
May my mind delight in the theater of Śrīraṅga. 2.
O abode of Lakṣmī, abode of the worlds, abode within the heart-lotus, abode within the solar orb,
abode in the ocean of milk, abode upon the coils of the serpent!
May my mind delight in dwelling at Śrīraṅga. 3.
O you who sport like Kubera, the sole plaything of the world; O you whose beautiful forehead is adorned with a garland of *mandāra* flowers;
O destroyer of the Daityas, the crown of all the worlds!
May my mind delight in the playful grace of Śrīraṅga. 4.
O Amoghanidrā, O sole sleep of the world,
O sleep of Videha, and O sleep of the ocean;
O Śrī-yoganidrā, O blissful Yoganidrā!
O Śrīraṅganidrā, may my mind take delight in you. 5.
In the form of bliss, in the form of innate consciousness, in the essential nature of Brahman, in the form of the earth,
in manifold forms, and in beautiful forms.
May my mind delight in the form of Śrīraṅga. 6.
O you who have fulfilled the purpose of your devotees, O enemy of Mura and Ravana,
O you who are capable for the sake of your devotees, O sole glory of the world,
O you of manifold forms, O you of beautiful form!
O Śrīraṅgamūrti, may my mind take delight in you. 7.
O crusher of Kaṃsa, crusher of Naraka,
crusher of the wicked, the source of the worlds;
O protector of the helpless, the sole lord of the universe!
May my mind delight in the Lord of Śrīraṅgam. 8.
He who sleeps on a beautiful bed, he who sleeps alone in the world, he who sleeps on the lap of Nanda, he who sleeps on the lap of Kamalā,
he who sleeps upon the ocean, and he who sleeps on a banyan leaf.
May He who reclines on the auspicious Raṅga delight my mind. 9.
The remover of all evils, the bearer away of the earth’s burden, the destroyer of the race of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, the dispeller of the pride of the Daityas;
he who performs most graceful movements and the snatcher away of the Pārijāta tree.
May the illustrious Murāri, who removes the fear of the three worlds, be pleased. 10.
If a person recites this meritorious hymn to Raṅga at dawn,
the sins accumulated over ten million lifetimes are destroyed by its mere remembrance.
Thus ends the Śrīraṅgastotra.
